title: Senior M&E Officer *2
description:
Position Overview: The Senior Monitoring and Evaluation (M&E) Officer will oversee monitoring, evaluation, data management, reporting, and information use activities under the Emergency Project and other related project at Koidu Government Hospital (KGH). The project supports Adult Emergency Services, Pediatric Ward, Pediatric Resuscitation, and other emergency care initiatives aimed at improving the quality, accessibility, and effectiveness of emergency health services as well as RMNACH program. Reporting to the Health Statistics Manager, the Senior M&E Officer will lead the data collection, analysis and continuous improvement of monitoring and evaluation systems to ensure the availability of accurate, timely, and high-quality data for program management, donor reporting, clinical decision-making, and health system strengthening. The position will provide direct supervision, mentorship, and technical support to M&E Officer(s), ensuring adherence to PIH standards, donor requirements, and Ministry of Health reporting guidelines. The Senior M&E Officer will serve as the primary focal point for donor reporting, stakeholder engagement, performance monitoring, data governance and quality assurance across the Emergency Project. Working closely with SHIS leadership, hospital management, clinical teams, Ministry of Health counterparts, and external partners, the role will promote a culture of data use and accountability by translating data into actionable insights that drive quality improvement, operational efficiency, and evidence-based decision-making. In addition, the Senior M&E Officer will support the design and implementation of data quality improvement initiatives, operational research activities, and performance review processes.

Essential Duties and Responsibilities:
1. Program Management - Contribute to the development and implementation of the overall M&E strategy for the Emergency Project. Develop and monitor annual M&E work plans and performance monitoring frameworks. Ensure alignment of indicators with donor requirements, PIH standards, and Ministry of Health requirements. Provide technical support to M&E Officers and M&E Assistants in overall WYSS projects related M&E activities. Serve as the principal M&E focal point for the WYSS grant.
2. Team Leadership and Supervision - Directly supervise M&E Officers and M&E Assistants assigned to the WYSS project. Conduct performance planning, coaching, mentorship, and annual performance evaluation of the team under his/her supervision. Review and approve technical reports, dashboards, analyses, and data products. Coordinate staff assignments and monitor deliverables.
3. Donor Reporting and Compliance - Take lead in the preparation and review of monthly, quarterly, semi-annual, and annual data donor reports and ensure compliance with donor reporting requirements and indicator definitions. Coordinate donor visits, audits, evaluations, performance reviews and adhoc data requests. Track progress against project targets and recommend corrective actions.
4. Capacity building - Build the technical capacity of M&E staff through structured mentorship and training. Provide feedback to M&E Officers and M&E Assistants on the quality of products being produced. Train service providers including nurses, clinicians, CHOs among others on data capturing and reporting requirements using both paper and electronic platforms.
5. Stakeholder Engagement and Coordination - Represent SHIS in project leadership meetings. Collaborate with hospital management, clinical leadership, Ministry of Health officials, and partners. Present project performance findings to senior leadership and donors. Strengthen coordination across Adult Emergency, Pediatric Ward, and Pediatric Resuscitation services.
6. Data Governance and Data Quality Assurance - Ensure adherence to SHIS data governance policies and procedures. Establish and maintain systems for routine data collection, validation, analysis, and reporting. Lead regular Data Quality Assessments (DQAs), data audits, and verification exercises. Ensure data completeness, accuracy, timeliness, consistency, and integrity across all emergency service programs. Strengthen electronic and paper-based data management systems and support continuous improvement initiatives. Develop standard operating procedures, tools, and guidelines for data management and reporting.
7. Data Analysis and use - Lead data analysis and interpretation to identify trends, gaps, and opportunities for program improvement. Develop and maintain Power BI dashboards and other visualization tools for emergency services. Support operational research, quality improvement initiatives, abstracts, publications, and dissemination of findings. Promote data use among clinicians, managers, and stakeholders to improve patient outcomes and service delivery.
8. Perform any other duties as assigned from time to time by supervisor and leadership (Clinical or SHIS).

Education and Work Experience Requirements:
Academic Qualification - Bachelor's degree in relevant field.
Technical Competencies - Minimum of five years of progressive experience in monitoring and evaluation, health information systems, or data management. At least two years of experience supervising technical staff. Demonstrated experience working with clinical/program staff in project management related activities. Advanced proficiency in Excel, Power BI, DHIS2, CommCare and data analysis tools. Strong experience in data quality assurance, data governance, and performance monitoring. Sound supervisory skills. Report-writing skills for internal use and donor requirements.
Behavioral Competencies - Professional, resourceful problem-solver, adapts well to changing priorities and demands, able to work well with ambiguity. Interpersonal skills - able to communicate effectively, active listener, highly collaborative, and provides constructive feedback. Detail oriented - strong attention to detail and commitment to getting it right, delivering polished, high-quality deliverables with minimal oversight. Ethical - Demonstrated alignment with and commitment to the health information professionals' code of ethics; data and information governance policies along with a natural passion for strengthening strategic health information system in Sierra Leone. Demonstrated passion for strengthening the health system in Sierra Leone and belief in giving a preferential option to the poor. Commitment to understanding and advocating for PIH's mission, strategy and approach to addressing health issues in settings of poverty.

Organisation Profile: Partners In Health (PIH) is a global health and social justice organization that responds to the moral imperative to provide high-quality health care globally to those who need it most. We currently work in 11 countries, including Sierra Leone, where we strive to ease suffering by placing patients at the center of all care, bringing the benefits of modern medicine to all.

Method of application: Interested candidates are required to apply through our website: www.pih.org/employment. In your application, please ensure to include names, addresses, email addresses and telephone numbers of three (3) referees not later than 12:00pm GMT (Midnight) on Wednesday, August 19th, 2026.

title: Enumerator
description:
Job Vacancy: Enumerators

Position Title: Enumerator

Location: Freetown & Out of Town

Contract Type: Short-term/Project-based

Reports To: Field Supervisor

About RAMLabs: RAMLabs (Research and Adaptive Monitoring Labs) is a research and advisory firm established in 2020 by West Africa–based researchers, specialising in cutting-edge social experiments, rigorous monitoring, evaluation and learning (MEL) systems, and programme quality improvement strategies. We work with leading international universities, NGOs, private sector actors and government ministries to design and implement high-quality studies and evaluations that inform policy and practice across sectors including health, education, livelihoods and urban resilience. As an enumerator, you will join a team that manages complex qualitative and quantitative data collection, supports innovative Randomised Control Trials and other field experiments, and contributes to evidence that shapes decisions in Sierra Leone and the wider region.

Position Overview: We are seeking motivated and detail-oriented Field Enumerators to support data collection activities for ongoing research projects. The role involves conducting interviews, facilitating discussions, and gathering accurate field data to inform program decisions.

Key Responsibilities:
- Conduct household and community interviews using structured questionnaires.
- Record responses accurately on digital devices.
- Ensure confidentiality and ethical handling of respondent information.
- Report daily progress and challenges to supervisors.
- Follow field protocols and instructions strictly.
- Conduct Key Informant Interviews (KIIs) with community leaders, stakeholders, and relevant institutions.
- Facilitate Focus Group Discussions (FGDs) with diverse participant groups, ensuring inclusivity and neutrality.

Qualifications & Requirements:
- Minimum of a Diploma or currently enrolled for a bachelor’s degree programme.
- Strong communication and interpersonal skills.
- Proficiency in English and local languages.
- Basic knowledge of smartphones/tablets for data entry.
- Prior experience in surveys or fieldwork is an advantage.
- Demonstrate flexibility and willingness to travel out of town for extended periods as required.
- Proven experience in conducting phone surveys and other data collection methods.
- Proficiency in local languages is an added advantage.

Terms of Employment:
- Remuneration: competitive
- Working Hours: Field-based, flexible depending on project needs.
- Other Benefits: transport and top up allowances

Application Process: Interested candidates should submit a CV/resume, copies of academic/professional certificates, and contact details of two referees.

Deadline for Applications: 23 August 2026

Apply Via: abarrie@ramlabs.org and cc agebeh@ramlabs.org

Equal Opportunity Statement: We value diversity and inclusion. All qualified applicants will be considered without regard to race, gender, disability, or religion.

Please note: Individuals who previously applied for this role should not apply again.

title: Senior M&E Officers – QEHSSSP
description:
PARTNERS IN HEALTH SIERRA LEONE, LLC. Job title: Senior M&E Officers – QEHSSSP. Department: Strategic Health Information System (SHIS). Reports to: Senior M&E Manager– QEHSSSP. Line Management: Yes. Duration of Contract: Twelve (12) Months. Application Status: Internal and External Advert. Req. No.: 4838.

Organization Profile: Partners In Health (PIH) is a global health and social justice organization committed to improving the health of people living in disadvantaged communities. PIH works in partnership with governments and communities to strengthen public health systems, expand access to high-quality care, address the social determinants of illness, and build the capacity of health workers and institutions. PIH began working in Sierra Leone during the 2014 Ebola response and has maintained a long-term commitment to strengthening the public health system. PIH-SL works with the Ministry of Health, district health management teams, health facilities, and communities, guided by public-sector accompaniment, equity, evidence-based practice, partnership, and community ownership.

Project and Position Overview: Under QEHSSSP, PIH-SL works with the Ministry of Health and district health management teams to strengthen essential health services, routine information systems, accountability, and the use of evidence for decision-making across supported districts and facilities. The Senior M&E Officer is the lead district-level focal point for project monitoring, data quality, analysis, reporting, learning, and performance review in Tonkolili. The post supports the District Medical Officer, DHMT M&E Coordinator, District Advisor, facility teams, and other project stakeholders to maintain reliable data systems and use findings to improve implementation. The role reports to the Senior M&E Manager – QEHSSSP and provides direct supervision, technical guidance, and coaching to assigned project M&E staff in the district. It does not replace the cross-district oversight responsibilities of the Senior M&E Manager.

Essential Duties and Responsibilities:
1. District M&E system implementation - Operationalize the approved project M&E plan, results framework, indicator reference sheets, reporting calendar, and data-flow procedures within Tonkolili District. Maintain district indicator trackers, targets, workplans, and action logs, and promptly escalate performance or reporting risks to the Senior M&E Manager and District Advisor. Coordinate routine data flow from supported PHUs, DHMT teams, and project workstreams to the district and central project levels.
2. Data collection, management, and reporting - Ensure routine project data are complete, timely, accurate, internally consistent, and supported by appropriate source documentation. Validate, consolidate, and submit district datasets and narrative reports in accordance with approved internal, government, and donor reporting schedules. Maintain secure, orderly, and auditable district M&E records, including databases, reporting tools, verification files, data dictionaries, and version-controlled submissions.
3. Data quality assurance - Plan and conduct routine data quality spot checks, data verification exercises, and formal DQAs at supported facilities and district level. Compare registers, tally sheets, patient records, reporting forms, electronic systems, and DHIS2 submissions to identify discrepancies and their root causes. Develop corrective action plans with responsible teams, track completion, and verify that recurring data quality problems are resolved.
4. Data analysis, visualization, and use - Analyse project performance by facility, geography, sex, age, service area, and other relevant disaggregation to identify trends, inequities, bottlenecks, and outliers. Develop and maintain clear dashboards, scorecards, charts, and performance briefs for project, DHMT, facility, and management review. Present findings in accessible language, support routine performance-review meetings, and translate analysis into specific recommendations and tracked actions. Contribute to project learning products, evaluation activities, operational research, and documentation of implementation lessons, as assigned.
5. Supervision and capacity strengthening - Provide line management and technical supervision to assigned project M&E staff, including work planning, task allocation, coaching, performance feedback, and follow-up on agreed deliverables. Assess M&E capacity gaps among project, DHMT, and facility teams and implement practical training, mentorship, and on-the-job coaching plans. Support consistent application of indicator definitions, data collection tools, data quality standards, analytical methods, and reporting formats across supported facilities.
6. Coordination, accountability, and other duties - Serve as the principal district M&E liaison among the DHMT, District Advisor, Senior M&E Manager, SHIS team, clinical and program leads, and relevant partners. Participate in project planning, supportive supervision, review meetings, audits, evaluations, and partner engagements, and follow through on agreed actions. Promote a culture of data use, accountability, respectful collaboration, safeguarding, and continuous improvement in all assigned work. Undertake other M&E-related duties reasonably assigned by the Senior M&E Manager or project leadership and consistent with the level and purpose of the role.

Prevention of Sexual Abuse and Exploitation: As a social justice organization, Partners in Health (PIH) is deeply committed to upholding the dignity and rights of the individuals and communities we serve. We recognize that many of the communities we work with are vulnerable, and it is our responsibility to prevent any form of sexual abuse or exploitation. We hold ourselves and all individuals associated with PIH accountable for reporting any allegations of sexual abuse or exploitation and enforcing consequences for such actions. Retaliation against individuals who report or participate in investigations will not be tolerated. We are dedicated to ensuring that our employees, volunteers, consultants, and all other representatives involved in delivering our services uphold these high standards and demonstrate respect and dignity towards all those impacted by our work.

Qualification and Experience:
Essential - Bachelor's degree in monitoring and evaluation, public health, epidemiology, biostatistics, statistics, demography, health informatics, social sciences, or another relevant discipline. At least three years of progressively responsible experience in monitoring, evaluation, health information, or data management, preferably within public health or a donor-funded programme. Demonstrated experience with indicator tracking, routine health data, data verification, DQAs, quantitative analysis, report writing, and presentation of findings. Strong working knowledge of Microsoft Excel and proficiency in Word and PowerPoint; practical experience with DHIS2 or comparable routine health information systems. Experience supervising or mentoring staff and building the M&E capacity of facility, district, or programme teams. Strong written and verbal communication skills, sound judgement, attention to detail, and the ability to manage competing deadlines with limited supervision. Ability and willingness to travel regularly to supported facilities, including PHUs in hard-to-reach locations within Tonkolili District.
Preferred - Postgraduate training in monitoring and evaluation, public health, epidemiology, biostatistics, health informatics, or a related field will be an added advantage. Experience using one or more analytical or visualization tools such as Power BI, Stata, R, SPSS, or advanced Excel, and digital data collection platforms such as KoboToolbox, ODK, or CommCare. Knowledge of Sierra Leone's national HMIS, district health structures, and Ministry of Health reporting processes. Proficiency in Krio and/or languages commonly spoken in Tonkolili District.
Core competencies - Technical rigour; Leadership and accountability; Collaboration; Problem-solving and adaptability; Integrity and confidentiality; Commitment to equity.

Social Justice: We are a global health and social justice organization that responds to the moral imperative to provide high-quality health care globally to those who need it most. We strive to ease suffering by placing patients at the center of all care, bringing the benefits of modern medicine to all.

Methods of Application: Interested candidates are required to apply through our website: www.pih.org/employment. In your application, please ensure to include names, addresses, email addresses and telephone numbers of three (3) referees not later than 12:00pm GMT (Midnight) on 26/08/2026. PIH is an equal opportunity employer and does not discriminate applicants on the basis of sex, religion, tribe or region. Female applicants are encouraged to apply and only shortlisted candidates will be contacted for an interview.

title: Back-up Medical Provider
description:
Back-up Medical Provider

Statement of Work
Organization: US Government – Peace Corps Sierra Leone
PSC Position Title: Back-up Medical Provider
Reports To: Country Director
Supervises: N/A
Contract Type: Long Term Intermittent, Not to Exceed 120 Calendar Days in a Calendar Year, Not to Exceed 40 Hours per Week
Duty Location: Freetown, Sierra Leone

Summary
Peace Corps Sierra Leone is seeking the services of up to two (2) qualified medical doctors to serve as the Back-up Medical Provider in the absence of the Peace Corps Medical Officer (PCMO) and provide support at peak times. The Back-up Medical Provider will deliver health care to U.S. Peace Corps Volunteers in Sierra Leone under the supervision of PCMOs.

The Back-up Medical Provider will deliver direct patient care, referrals to outside medical consultants or facilities, i.e., hospitals or emergency clinics depending on in-country arrangements and assist with administrative duties and health education when instructed.

When on duty, the Back-up Medical Provider will be available around-the-clock by telephone or be present in the Peace Corps office Health Unit. He/she may also be required to provide consultative or prescriptive services on behalf of PCMOs.

Responsibilities
- Routine primary health care to Peace Corps Trainees and Volunteers including treatment of common illnesses and injuries in accordance with Peace Corps medical guidelines.
- Individual short-term counseling on disease prevention, adjustment issues, stress management and cross-cultural problems
- Respond to emergency medical situations
- Conduct trainings on health care issues
- Site visits to Peace Corps Volunteers throughout Sierra Leone
- Administrative tasks of the medical office including budget management
- Inventory of medical supplies and equipment
- Alternate 24 hour on-call duty with other PCMOs

Requirements
- Graduate of accredited school. MDs must be a graduate of a school listed in the Foundation for Advancement of International Medical Education and Research at the following link https://search.wdoms.org/
- Current valid license to practice in Sierra Leone
- Relevant clinical experience in primary care after medical school. Proficiency in the assessment and management of acute and on-going illnesses.

Preferred Qualifications
- Ability to communicate effectively in English and Krio orally and in writing
- Experience in managing mental health issues including patience counseling
- Experience in training design and presentation of health-related materials
- Working knowledge of Microsoft Word, Excel, Outlook and other applications.
- Program management and administrative experience.
- Ability to work effectively as part of an intercultural team.
- Willing to travel within Sierra Leone.
- Ability to work with minimal supervision.
- Must be able to travel to Morrocco and security clearance.
- Must be able to legally work in Sierra Leone. Peace Corps will not process work permits.

Submission Requirements
The application deadline is August 28th, 2026, at 5:00PM.

In order to be considered for this position, the applicant must;
- Be a Sierra Leone Citizen with residency and must not have been employed in intelligence-related activities.
- Age requirement must be below legal retirement age in Sierra Leone (60 years)
- Submit complete application package on/before the application deadline date and time by email to: SL-pcjobs@peacecorps.gov or by hand to HR Specialist, Peace Corps Sierra Leone, 34 Old Railway Line, Signal Hill, Freetown
- Application must include the following;
  - A letter of interest addressing the required qualifications.
  - A complete CV, to include: All relevant employment, including start and end dates (month and year) for each position listed, and a summary of key tasks and responsibilities for each position; Educational background and a list of current license(s)/Certificates/degrees etc. held; Contact information of three professional references; Information regarding citizenship and work authorization in Sierra Leone.
- All education, experience, skills and qualifications will be verified.

All experience, skills, and qualifications will be verified. Applicants with high potential will be scheduled for an interview at the Peace Corps office in Freetown. Employment is contingent on a favorable security background and medical check.

Please include “Ref: “Peace Corps Back-up Medical Provider”” on the envelope submission and or in the subject line for the online application

title: Programme Development and Quality Co-ordinator
description: Concern Worldwide Sierra Leone is seeking a Programme Development and Quality Co-ordinator. Reports to: Programme Director. Direct reports: TBD. Liaises with: Program coordinator MEAL, all members of the Country project teams, Advocacy and communications manager, Area Coordinators. Job Location: Freetown, will be required to attend workshops or trainings and mandated to travel to the provinces for regular support. Contract Details: Fixed Term – 1 year. Job Purpose: The Programme Development and Quality Co-ordinator will manage the Program Development and Quality (PDQ) team to ensure high quality programming, programme design and learning through quantitative and qualitative monitoring and accountability to beneficiaries of Concern’s programmes, and coordinate implementation and maintenance of the country program learning agenda. Main duties & Responsibilities include: Programme development (support sector leads on expressions of interest, lead Go/No Go decision meetings, lead proposal development processes including proposal development plans, technical inputs, milestones, ensure Concern policies/strategies/guidelines followed, lead proposal development workshops, collaborate with partnerships coordinator to include local partners, build relationships with donors, track funding opportunities); Grant management (contribute to donor reports, quality assurance on data analysis and writing, support Grants and Compliance Manager with GMS system); Learning (develop knowledge management system, contribute to Digital Workplace and GMS, oversee documentation and sharing of programme impact/learning, ensure learning reviews conducted and documented, support coordination of learning activities, manage PDQ budgets, lead strategic project documentation); Equality, Diversity & Inclusion (drive integration of Gender & Equality in programmes, oversee Equality Action Plan implementation, support training on diversity/inclusion); Visibility (promote Concern's reputation externally); People management and Capacity Building (monitor/review supervisee performance, ensure compliance with policies, develop training on PCMS and PM&E tools, research and disseminate new approaches); Partnership and Localisation (mentor and provide technical advice to partners, facilitate trainings, support capacity assessments, review partner reports, support incorporation of learning, design training materials, ensure partner recognition in donor reports); Other Duties (participate in PEER/SMP updates, proposal development, strategic plan initiatives, promote Concern's reputation, ensure efficient/transparent use of resources, promote compliance with Code of Conduct, Programme Participants Protection Policy, Child Safeguarding Policy, Anti-trafficking Policy, Anti-Fraud Policy, CHS/CRM, promote Equality especially gender, undertake other duties as assigned). Person specification - Essentials: University degree in relevant field (communications, advocacy, M&E, development, inclusion); Minimum 3-5 years of experience in PDQ and minimum 2 years' experience line managing staff; Experience in capacity development of staff and partners; Clear understanding and vision for using community voices, data and information to support Programme learning and advocacy; Understanding and experience in gender equality and power dynamics; Experience managing and implementing primary qualitative data collection (KIIs, FGDs, participatory methods); Experience supporting proposal/project design (logframes/results frameworks); Excellent computer skills (Excel, Word, PowerPoint); Experience managing budgets; Excellent written and presenting skills in English; Able to work independently, multi-task, take initiative, delegate, and harness team efforts. Desirable: Experience with education, livelihoods, and health projects in Sierra Leone; Experience with emergency projects in Sierra Leone; Experience in program design. Also includes sections on Emergency response (staff required to participate in emergency responses) and Partnership and Localisation commitments. How to Apply: Submit application letter justifying suitability, CV with three referees (one being current/most recent employer), state referee positions/relationships, attach valid labour card, police clearance required from successful candidate, applications sent to info.sl@concern.net with reference in subject heading, copy of application letter also sent to NGO Desk Officer, Ministry of Labour & Social, New England or emailed to employmentdesk71@gmail.com. Closing date: 17:00 Wednesday 26th August 2026. Only shortlisted candidates contacted. Female candidates strongly encouraged to apply.

title: Head of Business Development
description:
ABOUT BEAM AND THE ROLE: Beam, a growing and dynamic enterprise under The Elba Group, is seeking an experienced and highly motivated Head of Business Development to lead growth across its diverse business areas. This role is ideal for a confident leader who enjoys building, creating, and delivering results. The Head of Business Development will be responsible for developing and implementing strategies to grow Beam’s business units, strengthen partnerships, expand markets, and increase revenue. The role requires a hands-on leader who is a creative and critical thinker, problem solver, and confident communicator.

WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR: A strong and inspiring leader who can guide and motivate a team; Confident and proactive, willing to make suggestions and challenge ideas constructively; A critical thinker and problem solver who turns challenges into opportunities; Self-driven, with the ability to use initiative and work independently; An excellent communicator, both verbally and in writing; Results-oriented, excited about delivering outcomes and seeing ideas through; Someone who loves their work and brings energy, commitment, and creativity to the role.

KEY RESPONSIBILITIES:
